# Inume Opencode Retro Themes

> 13 free, MIT-licensed retro themes for OpenCode, the open-source terminal AI coding agent (TUI), by Gianluca Bernasconi. Each theme recreates the look of classic hardware and software — Windows 95, Norton Commander, IBM phosphor terminals, CGA, PlayStation 1 and 2, GameCube, Game Boy, Famicom, SNES, PCB circuit boards, and worn neon. Works on OpenCode 1.x and 2.x; last tested with OpenCode 2.0.21 (October 2026).

Themes are JSON files dropped into `~/.config/opencode/themes/` and activated with `/themes` inside OpenCode (which opens the theme selector), or set as the default in `cli.json` with `"theme": { "name": "<name>" }` on OpenCode 2.x (`"theme": "<name>"` in `tui.json` on OpenCode 1.x).

Every theme is validated on each push: OpenCode theme $schema, all 50 color tokens with dark and light variants, and a 1.8:1 contrast floor for key text/background pairs (a legibility floor, not WCAG).

Install one theme without cloning (`theme-name` is any ID from the list below):

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/themes
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/main/themes/theme-name.json \
  -o ~/.config/opencode/themes/theme-name.json
```

## Key pages

- [README](https://github.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/blob/main/README.md): theme list, screenshot gallery, and installation (one-liner or install script)
- [Themes folder](https://github.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/tree/main/themes): the 13 JSON theme files
- [Install script](https://github.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/blob/main/install.sh): interactive installer (`./install.sh`, `./install.sh all`, or specific theme names), or `--project` to install into `./.opencode/themes`
- [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/): the terminal AI coding agent these themes target

## Themes

- [w95-classic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/main/themes/w95-classic.json): Windows 95 — teal desktop, gray panels (fixed palette)
- [norton-commander](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/main/themes/norton-commander.json): Norton Commander — blue file-manager terminal (fixed palette)
- [ibm-old-terminal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/main/themes/ibm-old-terminal.json): IBM PC terminal — green phosphor on black (fixed palette)
- [cga](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/main/themes/cga.json): CGA palette — early PC color, cyan/black (fixed palette)
- [theme-station-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/main/themes/theme-station-1.json): PlayStation 1 — pale gray shell
- [theme-station-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/main/themes/theme-station-2.json): PlayStation 2 — deep black, blue aura
- [theme-cube](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/main/themes/theme-cube.json): Nintendo GameCube — purple hardware
- [dot-matrix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/main/themes/dot-matrix.json): Nintendo Game Boy — four-shade pea-green LCD (fixed palette)
- [family-computheme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/main/themes/family-computheme.json): Nintendo Famicom — cream and red
- [super-theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/main/themes/super-theme.json): Super Nintendo — soft gray, purple accents (fixed palette)
- [super-color](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/main/themes/super-color.json): SNES multicolor — brighter palette (fixed palette)
- [silicon-trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/main/themes/silicon-trace.json): PCB circuits — chip traces, green board
- [faded-neon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gianlucabernasconi/Inume-Opencode-Retro-Themes/main/themes/faded-neon.json): worn neon — dim pink/green glow (fixed palette)
